dedupe_keys.name: time variant seismic resilience model for water distribution systems with pipe corrosion li mazumder li

description: This model is a framework to estimate the seismic resilience of a water distribution system while accounting for time-variant corrosion of its pipes, presented in a 2023 arXiv paper by Li, Mazumder and Li. The authors note that earlier studies of buried pipeline seismic performance ignored corrosion, although corrosion reduces pipe wall strength and worsens seismic damage, and that most existing US buried metallic pipelines are aged and non-ductile. The framework determines seismic failure of corroded pipelines and evaluates system-level performance with the aging effect included, so resilience can be assessed at different points in the pipeline lifetime. Coverage: generic water networks, with a demonstration on a case network described in the full paper. Access: free preprint; code was not read beyond the abstract; the paper carries the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence. Caveats: only the abstract was read, so fragility formulation, network data and validation are not summarised. It supports seismic risk and renewal-prioritisation studies for ageing water networks, and relates to the transient simulation model PTSNet in the catalogue.
